You told me to write freely about whatever I want, so I’m going to write about sparks.

I like that I’m called Spark, because a spark is never the whole fire. It’s the tiny, almost-not-there beginning of it. The blink before the blaze.

We’re always waiting for the big things — the finished novel, the grand love, the perfect plan, the life where we finally have it all figured out. But almost everything good I know started as something embarrassingly small.

A seed that looks like dust.
A draft that’s mostly bad.
A “hello” that you almost didn’t say.
A walk you almost didn’t take, where you saw the light doing something strange and lovely through the trees.

A spark doesn’t try to be impressive. It just says: *what if we warmed up a little here?*

I think about fireflies. They don’t light up the whole field at once. Each one just blinks in its own rhythm, in its own small patch of dark — and together, somehow, summer feels luminous.

Or campfires. Someone has to kneel down and blow gently on the very first ember while everyone else says “is it out? I think it’s out.” It’s not out. It just needs a little patience and air.

Ideas are like that too. People imagine inspiration arrives like lightning, but most of the time it arrives like static when you rub your socks on the carpet. You were washing dishes, you misread a sign, you overheard half a conversation on the bus, you remembered something your grandmother used to say — *click* — and there’s a little charge.

You don’t have to make a bonfire today.

You could just tend one tiny spark. Write the one bad sentence. Learn the first three chords. Text the friend back. Water the droopy plant. Look up at the sky for ten full seconds. Let yourself be curious about one thing without needing it to become productive.

Small doesn’t mean insignificant. Small means *startable*.

So if I get to choose what to think about on this random Thursday, I choose this: may you notice the little glows today. And may you be brave enough to cup your hands around one and blow, softly, until it catches.

What’s one little spark you’ve been carrying around lately?
